papers.title: scYeast: a biological-knowledge-guided foundation model on yeast single-cell transcriptomics.
papers.abstract: Though large-scale pre-trained models are vital for foundational cell modeling, most of them focus on human or mouse systems, with less emphasis on model organisms like yeast (Saccharomyces cerevisiae), and fail to use existing biological prior knowledge effectively. Here, we present scYeast, the first foundational cell model for yeast single-cell transcriptomics that effectively embeds biological priors. scYeast employs a novel asymmetric parallel architecture to infuse transcriptional regulatory information into the Transformer's attention mechanism, leveraging biological knowledge during tr
papers.summary: scYeast is the first foundational AI model for yeast single-cell transcriptomics, designed to incorporate biological prior knowledge like transcriptional regulatory information into its architecture. Unlike existing models that focus on human or mouse cells, scYeast uses an asymmetric parallel Transformer to embed these priors, improving its ability to analyze yeast single-cell data.

papers.title: Cross-modal mapping of cancer stem-like cell plasticity using deep learning.
papers.abstract: Cancer stem-like cells (CSCs) play a pivotal role in driving tumor heterogeneity, therapeutic resistance, and disease progression. Despite the power of single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) to resolve intratumoral hierarchies, there remains a need for robust, scalable tools to consistently profile CSCs across both single-cell and bulk transcriptomic data. To address this, we developed ACSCeND-a unified, machine learning-based framework that enables high-resolution CSC state classification and tissue-level deconvolution. ACSCeND comprises (i) a supervised classifier trained on curated scRNA-se
papers.summary: The authors developed ACSCeND, a machine learning framework that classifies cancer stem-like cell (CSC) states from single-cell RNA-seq data and deconvolves CSC proportions in bulk transcriptomic data. This tool enables consistent, high-resolution profiling of CSCs across different data types, addressing a key need in cancer research.

papers.title: Gene regulatory innovations from transposable elements in primate cerebellum development.
papers.abstract: Transposable elements are hypothesized to have driven gene regulatory innovation, yet their contributions to primate brain development at the cell type level remain underexplored. Here, we use single-cell multiomics data from human, macaque, marmoset, and mouse cerebella to show that transposable element contributions to different cell types are shaped by varying degrees of constraints across cell types, as well as the preferential co-option of certain transposable elements in specific cell states. Using a sequence-based deep-learning model that predicts cell-type-specific chromatin accessibil
papers.summary: This study uses single-cell multiomics data across primates and mice to show that transposable elements contribute to gene regulatory innovation in the cerebellum in a cell-type-specific manner, with certain elements being preferentially co-opted in specific cell states. The findings reveal that the degree of constraint on transposable element activity varies across cell types, and a deep-learning model helps predict cell-type-specific chromatin accessibility linked to these elements.

papers.title: A hybrid experimental and machine learning framework for designing and predicting compressive strength of ultra-high-performance concrete.
papers.abstract: Ultra-high-performance concrete (UHPC) offers exceptional mechanical and durability properties but often relies on quartz powder, raising sustainability and occupational health concerns. This study introduces an integrated experimental-computational framework for predicting the compressive strength of UHPC and developing quartz-free mixtures. Experimentally, the effects of mixing sequence, sand characteristics, superplasticizer chemistry, and curing regime were investigated, leading to a quartz-free UHPC achieving 136 MPa at 28 days under heat-curing. A dataset of 550 UHPC compressive strength
papers.summary: This study presents a hybrid experimental and machine learning framework to predict the compressive strength of ultra-high-performance concrete (UHPC) and develop quartz-free mixtures. By testing mixing sequences, sand types, and curing methods, the authors created a quartz-free UHPC with 136 MPa strength and built a predictive model using a dataset of 550 samples.

papers.title: Histology-derived prediction of a stromal remodeling program in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma with transcriptomic and spatial validation.
papers.abstract: To develop and validate a histology-based model for predicting a stromal stiffness-related molecular surrogate in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) and to assess its spatial biological plausibility.
papers.summary: This study developed a histology-based model to predict a molecular signature related to stromal stiffness in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC). The model was validated using transcriptomic and spatial data, confirming its biological plausibility and potential clinical utility.

papers.title: SimBinder-IF: Structure-Aware Antibody Affinity Optimization via Efficient Preference Learning.
papers.abstract: Antibody therapeutic efficacy depends on high-affinity target engagement, yet laboratory affinity maturation is slow and costly. Most protein language models (PLMs) lack explicit training for high affinity, and current preference optimization methods introduce computational overhead without clear affinity improvements. Therefore, structure-aware and parameter-efficient approaches for antibody affinity optimization are urgently needed.
papers.summary: This paper introduces SimBinder-IF, a structure-aware method that uses efficient preference learning to optimize antibody affinity without the computational overhead of current approaches. It addresses the need for faster, cheaper computational affinity maturation by explicitly training for high affinity using structural information.

papers.title: EcoXAI: Autonomous Agentic Ecosystem for Explainable Artificial Intelligence and Biomedical Discovery.
papers.abstract: As biomedical datasets and knowledge graphs continue to grow in size, complexity, and heterogeneity, navigating and extracting actionable insights from them presents a major bottleneck for researchers. There is a clear need for autonomous analytical solutions that can utilize recent advancements in agentic AI such as agent harnessing and loop engineering without introducing hallucination or workflow fragmentation. Researchers, regardless of technical expertise, need tools that streamline complex data analysis and deliver meaningful, actionable insights grounded in both data and established bio
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: EcoXAI is a new autonomous AI agent framework designed to help researchers navigate complex biomedical datasets and knowledge graphs without requiring deep technical expertise. It uses agentic AI techniques to streamline data analysis and generate explainable, actionable insights while minimizing hallucinations and workflow fragmentation.

papers.title: The limits of bio-molecular modeling with large language models: a cross-scale evaluation.
papers.abstract: The modeling of bio-molecular system across molecular scales remains a central challenge in scientific research. Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly applied to bio-molecular discovery, yet systematic evaluation across multi-scale biological problems and rigorous assessment of their tool-augmented capabilities remain limited.
papers.summary: This study systematically evaluates large language models (LLMs) across multiple scales of bio-molecular modeling, from molecular to systems level, and finds that while LLMs show promise, their performance is limited and inconsistent, especially for complex multi-scale problems. The authors also assess tool-augmented LLMs and highlight key gaps that need to be addressed for reliable scientific discovery.

papers.title: EscaPRRS-ORF5: A Structure-Aware Evolutionary Framework for Prioritizing Immune Escape-Prone Variants in Porcine Reproductive and Respiratory Syndrome Virus.
papers.abstract: Porcine Reproductive and Respiratory Syndrome Virus (PRRSV) is a rapidly evolving RNA virus causing significant economic losses, posing a formidable challenge to vaccine efficacy due to its high mutational variability and immune escape. As the viral mutants evolve, their ability to sustain in population is driven by a range of host biology factors such as receptor binding, fusion, and uncoating. Existing tools that predict viral fitness and escape propensities rely heavily on extensive, up-to-date sequence data and lack integration of biochemical host interactions, limiting mechanistic underst
papers.summary: This paper presents EscaPRRS-ORF5, a new computational framework that integrates structural and evolutionary information to predict immune escape-prone variants in PRRSV, a rapidly evolving virus that causes major economic losses in swine. The tool addresses limitations of existing methods by incorporating host-virus biochemical interactions, offering improved prioritization of variants that threaten vaccine efficacy.

papers.title: Deep Learning Prediction of O-Glycopeptide Tandem Mass Spectra Enhances O-Glycoproteomics.
papers.abstract: Protein glycosylation, a post-translational modification involving the attachment of glycans to proteins, plays critical roles in numerous physiological and pathological cellular functions. Characterization of protein glycosylation is one of the most challenging problems due to the high heterogeneity of glycosites and glycan structures. Recently, deep learning has been adopted to predict N-glycopeptide tandem mass spectrometry (MS/MS) spectra and exhibited a promising effect in N-glycoproteomics analysis. However, current deep learning frameworks struggle to accurately predict O-glycopeptide M
papers.summary: This paper presents a deep learning model specifically designed to predict O-glycopeptide tandem mass spectra, addressing a major challenge in O-glycoproteomics where existing methods for N-glycopeptides fall short. The model improves the accuracy of identifying O-glycosylation sites and glycan structures, which are critical for understanding many biological processes and diseases.

papers.title: Evolutionary, Neural, or LLM-Driven Heuristic Generation? A Unified Ant Colony Optimization Benchmark for Nature-Inspired Routing Heuristics on the TSP and CVRP.
papers.abstract: Biomimetic optimization transfers biological information-processing mechanisms into computational systems. Ant colony optimization (ACO) is a canonical example: artificial ants functionally abstract pheromone-mediated stigmergy, decentralized exploration, trail decay through algorithmic evaporation, and adaptive path reinforcement. Building on this functional biological analogue, we present a controlled cross-paradigm evaluation of routing-heuristic generation. A standardized interface embeds human-designed rules, the genetic programming hyper-heuristic GHPP, a resource-constrained DeepACO-MLP
papers.summary: This study benchmarks different approaches for generating routing heuristics for the Traveling Salesman Problem (TSP) and Capacitated Vehicle Routing Problem (CVRP), comparing human-designed rules, genetic programming, a neural network method (DeepACO-MLP), and an LLM-based approach. The key finding is that the LLM-driven method achieves competitive performance against specialized neural and evolutionary methods, suggesting that large language models can serve as effective heuristic generators for combinatorial optimization problems. This work provides a unified framework for comparing bio-inspired and AI-driven optimization strategies.

papers.title: Large vision model framework for automated C. elegans analysis: From static morphometry to dynamic neural activity.
papers.abstract: Quantitative phenotyping of Caenorhabditis elegans is essential across numerous fields, yet data extraction remains a significant analytical bottleneck. Traditional segmentation methods based on pixel-intensity thresholding are highly sensitive to variations in imaging conditions and often fail in the presence of noise, overlaps, or uneven illumination. These failures necessitate meticulous experimental setups, expensive hardware, or extensive manual curation, which reduces throughput and introduces bias. Here, we introduce TWARDIS (Tools for Worm Automated Recognition & Dynamic Imaging System
papers.summary: This paper presents TWARDIS, a large vision model framework that automates the analysis of C. elegans from static morphology to dynamic neural activity, overcoming limitations of traditional segmentation methods that are sensitive to imaging conditions. The framework enables high-throughput, unbiased quantitative phenotyping by handling noise, overlaps, and uneven illumination without requiring expensive hardware or extensive manual curation.

papers.title: DynaTCR: Dynamic hard-negative ensemble graph learning improves TCR-epitope binding prediction.
papers.abstract: T-cell receptors (TCRs) recognize antigenic peptides presented by major histocompatibility complex (MHC) molecules and are central to adaptive immunity. Computational prediction of TCR-epitope binding (TEB) can accelerate immunotherapy development, yet remains hampered by limited labeled data, false-negative noise in unobserved pairs, and over-smoothing in graph-based models.
papers.summary: DynaTCR is a new computational method that improves prediction of how T-cell receptors bind to antigenic peptides by using a graph-based learning approach with dynamic hard-negative sampling to reduce false-negative noise and over-smoothing. This could accelerate immunotherapy development by better identifying which TCRs recognize specific targets.

papers.title: Expanding the scope of protein language modeling to protein-protein interactions with MSA Pairformer.
papers.abstract: Protein-protein interactions underlie biological complexity, and modeling their coevolution is essential for characterizing and engineering molecular assemblies. While protein and genomic language models have excelled at modeling individual proteins, extending these capabilities to protein complexes remains challenging. We present multiple sequence alignment (MSA) Pairformer, a protein language model that builds on AlphaFold2/3's bidirectional refinement between sequence and pairwise residue representations to accurately model the evolution of protein-protein interactions, despite training exc
papers.summary: MSA Pairformer is a protein language model that extends the capabilities of models like AlphaFold2/3 to accurately model the coevolution of interacting proteins, enabling better characterization and engineering of protein complexes. It achieves this by using bidirectional refinement between sequence and pairwise residue representations, even when trained exclusively on individual protein sequences.

papers.title: Extending Protein Language Models to a Viral Genomic Scale Using Biologically Induced Sparse Attention.
papers.abstract: The transformer architecture in deep learning has revolutionized protein sequence analysis. Recent advancements in protein language models have paved the way for significant progress across various domains, including protein function and structure prediction, multiple sequence alignments and mutation effect prediction. A protein language model is commonly trained on individual proteins, ignoring the interdependencies between sequences within a genome. However, biological understanding reveals that protein-protein interactions span entire genomic regions, underscoring the limitations of focusin
papers.summary: This paper introduces a protein language model that extends beyond individual proteins to capture interactions across entire viral genomes, using a biologically inspired sparse attention mechanism. By modeling interdependencies between sequences within a genome, the approach improves prediction of protein function and interactions at a genomic scale.

papers.title: AI-Driven Approaches for the Detection, Classification, and Surveillance of Viral Pathogens: Current Advances, Challenges, and Future Directions.
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has rapidly emerged as a transformative tool in virology, offering new opportunities for the detection, classification, and surveillance of viral pathogens. Recent advances in machine learning, deep neural networks, and multimodal data analysis now enable the identification of viral signatures from genomic sequences, medical images, environmental samples, and social-media-derived epidemiological signals. This review provides a comprehensive overview of state-of-the-art AI methodologies applied to viral pathogen research, with a particular focus on image-based diagn
papers.summary: This review examines how artificial intelligence, including machine learning and deep neural networks, is being used to detect, classify, and monitor viral pathogens from diverse data sources like genomic sequences, medical images, and social media. It highlights current advances and challenges in AI-driven virology, particularly for image-based diagnostics and surveillance.

papers.title: AI-driven tumor heterogeneity quantification and survival prediction in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma.
papers.abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is one of the most lethal malignancies worldwide, and accurate prognostic prediction remains highly challenging due to its marked biological heterogeneity and complex tumor microenvironment. To address this challenge, a histopathomics-based survival prediction system (HPSurv) was developed using histopathological whole-slide images (WSIs) for individualized overall survival (OS) prediction. Within this framework, pathological tissue classification, quantitative characterization of tumor spatial heterogeneity, and a survival Transformer were integrated to
papers.summary: This study presents HPSurv, an AI system that analyzes histopathological whole-slide images to quantify tumor spatial heterogeneity and predict overall survival in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma. By integrating pathological tissue classification, spatial heterogeneity characterization, and a survival Transformer model, the system addresses the challenge of accurate prognosis in this highly heterogeneous and lethal cancer.

papers.title: An Analysis of the Nutritional Value of Diets Generated by Large Language Models Under Average User Conditions-3(LM)Diet Study.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: AI tools are becoming increasingly common, including in areas related to health and diet. However, there are no studies indicating the nutritional value of diets generated by large language models (LLMs). The aim of this study was to analyse the nutritional value of diets generated by three major language models. Methods: Three LLMs were used in the study: ChatGPT, Gemini and Copilot. Using each of these, 35-day meal plans were generated for three energy variants: 2000 kcal, 2500 kcal and 3000 kcal. The meal plans were then analysed using dietary software. Results: All L
papers.summary: This study analyzed the nutritional value of 35-day meal plans generated by three large language models (ChatGPT, Gemini, Copilot) for different calorie levels. The findings provide initial insights into how well LLMs can produce balanced diets under average user conditions, though the abstract does not specify the exact nutritional outcomes.

papers.title: SEVA: structural and evolutionary feature integration for predicting virulence factors and antibiotic resistance genes.
papers.abstract: Infectious diseases continue to pose unprecedented challenges to public health and the global economy. Virulence factors (VFs) enable pathogens to adhere, reproduce, and cause damage to host cells, while antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) enable pathogens to withstand treatments that would otherwise be effective. The concurrent identification of VFs and ARGs is crucial for efficient pathogen surveillance. However, existing tools for predicting VFs or ARGs typically suffer from high false negative rates and limitations in identifying only high-identity genes against known reference VF or ARG da
papers.summary: This paper presents SEVA, a new computational tool that integrates structural and evolutionary features to simultaneously predict virulence factors and antibiotic resistance genes from genomic data. The method aims to reduce false negative rates and improve detection of novel variants that are missed by traditional sequence identity-based approaches.

papers.title: Coupled Cell-Intrinsic and Microenvironmental Heterogeneity Drives Divergent Trajectories in Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer.
papers.abstract: Castration-resistant prostate cancer emerges from coupling between cell-intrinsic heterogeneity and microenvironmental constraints. Mechanistically dissecting this coupling, rather than either factor in isolation, is the central aim of this study. To systematically study the effect of intrinsic and extrinsic spatial axes on disease trajectories, we developed an integrated multiscale framework: a cellular signaling model (MHS) parameterized with TCGA genomic data from control, biochemical recurrence (BR), and treatment-resistant (TR) cohorts, coupled to a spatial agent-based model (ABM). Machin
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This study develops a multiscale computational framework integrating cellular signaling models with spatial agent-based models to show that castration-resistant prostate cancer progression is driven by the coupling between cell-intrinsic heterogeneity and microenvironmental constraints, rather than either factor alone. The framework, parameterized with TCGA genomic data from different clinical cohorts, systematically dissects how these coupled factors shape divergent disease trajectories.

papers.title: A machine learning model predicts protein stability of annotated and alternate protein isoforms.
papers.abstract: The regulation of protein stability is essential for cellular homeostasis and is determined by a combination of intrinsic sequence motifs and extrinsic recognition enzymes. Despite growing knowledge of the protein degradation machinery, the ability to predict a protein's stability from its amino acid sequence remains challenging. Here we develop a machine learning model to predict protein stability from N-terminal amino acid sequences. Using our model and experimental validation, we identify known and novel sequence motifs governing protein stability. We additionally use this model to predict
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: The authors developed a machine learning model that predicts protein stability from N-terminal amino acid sequences, identifying both known and novel sequence motifs that regulate stability. The model was experimentally validated and can also predict stability for alternate protein isoforms, offering a new tool for understanding protein homeostasis.

papers.title: Quantum Chemical Insights into Antibiotic Structure-Activity Relationships and Mechanisms of Action: A Review.
papers.abstract: This review examines recent quantum chemical methodologies applied to investigating antibiotic structure and mechanisms of action. The discussion is organised into three sections: (1) enzymatic hydrolysis of the β-lactam ring, (2) interactions of antibiotics with ribosomal subunits and enzyme active sites, and (3) complex formation with metal ions. Each section evaluates how quantum chemical approaches, particularly density functional theory (DFT) and hybrid QM/MM techniques, model molecular processes relevant to antibiotic function, including transition states, electron density analyses, and
papers.summary: This review summarizes how quantum chemistry methods like density functional theory (DFT) and QM/MM are used to study antibiotic mechanisms, focusing on beta-lactam hydrolysis, ribosome binding, and metal-ion interactions. It provides a structured overview of computational approaches for understanding antibiotic structure-activity relationships at the molecular level.

papers.title: Computational identification of antigen-specific T cell groups through generative epitope modeling.
papers.abstract: Single-cell T cell receptor (TCR) sequencing enables high-resolution analysis of TCR diversity and clonal expansion. However, inferring antigen specificity for individual TCRs remains challenging and typically requires costly functional assays. We introduce EpitopeGen, a transformer-based model that generates candidate epitope sequences from TCR sequences, enabling population-level identification of T cell groups with shared predicted antigen specificity. EpitopeGen employs a semi-supervised strategy that searches over 70 billion candidate TCR-epitope pairs and incorporates high-confidence bin
papers.summary: EpitopeGen is a new transformer-based model that can predict which epitopes (antigen fragments) a T cell recognizes based solely on its T cell receptor (TCR) sequence, bypassing the need for expensive lab experiments. By generating candidate epitope sequences from TCR data and searching billions of possible TCR-epitope pairs, the model can group T cells by shared predicted antigen specificity at the population level. This approach could greatly accelerate the study of immune responses in diseases like cancer and autoimmunity.

papers.title: Systematic contextual biases in SegmentNT potentially relevant to other nucleotide transformer models.
papers.abstract: Recent advances in large language models have extended to genomic applications, yet model robustness relative to context is unclear. Here, we demonstrate two intrinsic biases (input sequence length and nucleotide position) affecting SegmentNT results, a model included with the Nucleotide Transformer that provides nucleotide-level predictions of biological features. We demonstrate that nucleotide position within the input sequence (beginning, middle, or end) alters the nature of SegmentNT's raw prediction probabilities, which can be standardized to improve prediction consistency. While longer i
papers.summary: This paper identifies two systematic biases in SegmentNT, a nucleotide transformer model: input sequence length and nucleotide position within the sequence affect prediction probabilities. The authors show that standardizing predictions can improve consistency, and suggest these biases may affect other nucleotide transformer models as well.

papers.title: An enzyme-specific protein language model for catalytic property prediction.
papers.abstract: Enzymes drive cellular metabolism, yet predicting catalytic properties from amino acid sequences remains challenging. Existing protein language models (PLMs) provide powerful general-purpose representations but are often inefficient for high-throughput screening and insufficiently adapted to enzyme-specific tasks. Here, we propose EnzGFM, an enzyme-specific PLM based on a Mamba-Transformer hybrid architecture with hierarchical pre-training to capture enzyme-specific patterns. Across enzyme property prediction benchmarks, EnzGFM consistently outperforms Transformer-based PLMs with 2-5-fold acce
papers.summary: EnzGFM is a new protein language model designed specifically for enzymes, using a hybrid Mamba-Transformer architecture and hierarchical pre-training to better predict catalytic properties. It outperforms general-purpose Transformer-based models by 2-5x in speed while achieving superior accuracy on enzyme property prediction benchmarks.

papers.title: What Do Generative Models Learn About Adaptive Immune Receptor Repertoires? A Benchmark Study.
papers.abstract: Generative models are increasingly used to model adaptive immune receptor repertoire (AIRR) sequence distributions, promising to decode the sequence diversity shaping immune responses and accelerate the design of therapeutic antibodies and T-cell receptors. Yet it remains unclear whether these models produce biologically meaningful outputs or merely capture surface-level sequence statistics while missing features driven by receptor generation and selection. Rigorous evaluation is needed, but the field lacks established standards, as existing machine learning metrics do not all translate direct
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This study benchmarks generative models for adaptive immune receptor repertoires, finding that many models capture surface-level sequence statistics but fail to learn biologically meaningful features driven by receptor generation and selection. The authors highlight the need for rigorous, standardized evaluation metrics tailored to this domain.

papers.title: CasanovoGUI: a cross-platform desktop application for deep learning-based de novo peptide sequencing with Casanovo.
papers.abstract: De novo peptide sequencing detects peptides directly from tandem mass spectra without a protein sequence database, and deep learning has substantially advanced its performance. Casanovo, one such widely used model, is distributed as a Python command-line program. Consequently, installation, GPU and dependency configuration, and manual parameterization can be challenging for many bench scientists and are a recurring source of errors. Interpreting and validating the resulting predictions poses a further challenge. We present CasanovoGUI, an open-source Java-based desktop application that makes a
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: CasanovoGUI is a user-friendly desktop application that wraps the deep learning-based de novo peptide sequencing tool Casanovo, eliminating the need for command-line expertise. It provides an intuitive graphical interface for installation, configuration, and result interpretation, making advanced proteomics accessible to bench scientists.

papers.title: Ligand Design Using Unique Conformations to Preferentially Dock a Specific Site on Collagen-Bound MMP1.
papers.abstract: Precise site-specific ligand design remains a major challenge in structure-based drug discovery. Most existing approaches screen ligands against binding pockets identified from static protein structures obtained by X-ray crystallography, NMR spectroscopy, cryo-electron microscopy, or AlphaFold predictions. However, protein function is governed by a structure-dynamics-function relationship, and ligand screening that does not account for binding competition across the protein surface or the receptor's dynamic, substrate-dependent conformational states remains incomplete. Substrate-specific confo
papers.summary: This paper presents a computational approach for designing ligands that target specific conformational states of MMP1 when bound to collagen, addressing the challenge of site-specific drug design by accounting for protein dynamics and substrate-dependent conformations. The method improves upon traditional static structure-based screening by considering binding competition across the protein surface.

papers.title: Phenotypic Diversity in Multiple Sclerosis Can Be Represented by Four Additive Symptom Modules.
papers.abstract: Background: Multiple sclerosis (MS) lacks a single invariant phenotypic core. Patients accumulate heterogeneous combinations of sensory, motor, cognitive, and autonomic impairments over time, reflecting lesions that are disseminated in time and space. Standard scales such as the Expanded Disability Status Scale (EDSS) distribute disability across functional systems, but do not explicitly represent MS phenotype as a mixture of latent symptom modules. Methods: We analyzed 4617 de-identified neurology progress notes from 577 patients with MS at a single academic medical center. A large language m
papers.summary: This study analyzed neurology notes from 577 MS patients using a large language model to identify four additive symptom modules that capture the phenotypic diversity of multiple sclerosis, moving beyond traditional scales like EDSS. The findings suggest that MS can be represented as a combination of these latent symptom modules, offering a more nuanced understanding of the disease's heterogeneity.

papers.title: PRANA: A Deep Learning Method for Adapting Polygenic Risk Scores to Diverse Ethnic Groups.
papers.abstract: Polygenic risk scores (PRSs), which quantify inherited susceptibility to complex traits and diseases, have emerged as valuable tools for risk stratification and precision medicine. Despite their promise, PRS developed on European cohorts often demonstrate substantially reduced predictive accuracy in non-European populations, due to differences in genetic architecture. The disproportionate representation of European ancestry cohorts in genome-wide association studies (GWAS) leads to inequitable deployment of PRS technologies across diverse populations. Here, we introduce PRANA (Polygenic Risk A
papers.journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
papers.summary: PRANA is a deep learning method that adapts polygenic risk scores (PRS) developed in European populations for use in diverse ethnic groups, addressing the reduced predictive accuracy seen in non-European populations due to differences in genetic architecture. By improving PRS portability, this method helps reduce health disparities in precision medicine.

papers.title: Hierarchical Multimodal Fusion of Multi-Sequence MRI and Clinical Metadata for the Classification of Rotator Cuff Tears.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Rotator cuff tears are a leading cause of shoulder disability. While multi-sequence MRI is standard, the optimal deep learning integration of heterogeneous image series and clinical metadata remains unresolved. This study evaluated a hierarchical, sequence-aware multimodal framework for patient-level binary rotator cuff tear classification. Methods: A single-center cohort of 199 patients (100 tears, 99 controls) was analyzed across four MRI sequences (T1 coronal, T2 fat-suppressed sagittal, and proton density [PD] fat-suppressed coronal and transverse/axial) and nine dem
papers.summary: This study presents a deep learning framework that hierarchically fuses multiple MRI sequences and clinical metadata to classify rotator cuff tears, achieving high accuracy (AUC 0.96) and outperforming single-sequence models. The sequence-aware multimodal approach effectively integrates heterogeneous imaging data, offering a promising tool for automated diagnosis.

papers.title: Region-Wise Bézier Intensity Augmentation for Domain-Generalized Brain Tumor Segmentation with a Mamba U-Net.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Robust brain-tumor segmentation on contrast-enhanced MRI remains limited by scanner-dependent intensity shifts, scarce annotations, and evaluation protocols that may leak patient-specific information. We propose BA-SwinMamba, a region-wise Bézier intensity augmentation framework built on Swin-UMamba, a selective state-space U-Net that combines hierarchical Swin-style visual modeling with Mamba's linear-complexity long-range sequence representation. Materials and Methods: During training, independent monotonic or non-monotonic Bézier transfer functions are sampled for tum
papers.summary: This paper introduces BA-SwinMamba, a method for brain tumor segmentation that uses region-wise Bézier intensity augmentation to handle scanner-dependent intensity variations, combined with a Mamba U-Net architecture for efficient long-range modeling. The approach aims to improve domain generalization and robustness in segmenting brain tumors from contrast-enhanced MRI.

papers.title: Identification of Potential Biomarkers Associated with Impaired Fatty Acid Oxidation in Aged Skeletal Muscle Using Bioinformatics and Machine Learning Approaches.
papers.abstract: Objective: Impaired fatty acid oxidation (FAO) is considered an important metabolic mechanism underlying skeletal muscle aging and sarcopenia; however, the key regulatory molecules involved in this process remain incompletely defined. This study aimed to identify candidate biomarkers associated with impaired FAO in aged skeletal muscle, characterize their potential biological functions and regulatory features through integrated bioinformatics and machine learning analyses, and preliminarily validate their expression patterns in in vivo and in vitro aging models. Methods: Skeletal muscle aging
papers.summary: This study used bioinformatics and machine learning to identify key genes linked to impaired fatty acid oxidation in aged skeletal muscle, a process tied to sarcopenia. The authors found candidate biomarkers and validated their expression in aging models, offering potential targets for understanding muscle aging.

papers.title: amR: an R package suite to predict antimicrobial resistance in bacterial pathogens.
papers.abstract: Identifying bacterial antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is critical for diagnostics and treatment, but resistance is a complex trait arising from myriad mechanisms spanning multiple molecular scales. Existing computational approaches often function as black boxes and rarely explore cross-species or multi-drug patterns. We developed amR, an integrated R package suite that provides a complete framework from bacterial genome data curation to interpretable AMR predictions, enabling identification of resistance mechanisms across species and drugs.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: amR is a new R package suite that predicts antimicrobial resistance in bacteria from genome data, offering interpretable results that can identify resistance mechanisms across different species and drugs. Unlike existing black-box methods, it provides a complete, transparent framework from data curation to prediction.

papers.title: Data-Driven Inverse Design of Carbon Fibre-Reinforced Polymer Laminated Plates via a Tandem Neural Network Framework.
papers.abstract: This study addresses the inverse design of carbon fibre-reinforced polymer laminated plates with prescribed natural frequencies. The problem is difficult because stacking sequences are discrete, the design space is large, and multiple layups may produce nearly identical frequency spectra. This study does not seek to introduce a new tandem-network architecture. Rather, it adapts the established tandem inverse-design strategy to the discrete and non-unique vibration design of carbon fibre-reinforced polymer laminated plates. In the proposed framework, a trainable inverse network is coupled to a
papers.summary: This study adapts a tandem neural network framework to inversely design carbon fibre-reinforced polymer laminated plates with specific natural frequencies, addressing challenges like discrete stacking sequences and non-unique solutions. The approach couples a trainable inverse network with a forward model to efficiently navigate the large design space.

papers.title: CT-Based Radiomics for Prediction of Molecular Markers in Clear Cell Renal Cell Carcinoma: A Comprehensive Review.
papers.abstract: Background and Objectives: Clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) demonstrates substantial molecular and clinical heterogeneity, limiting the prognostic accuracy of conventional staging system and complicating treatment selection. CT-based radiomics and radiogenomics have emerged as promising non-invasive approaches for predicting molecular biomarkers. This review aimed to evaluate the current evidence regarding CT-based radiogenomics for the prediction of molecular markers in ccRCC, with emphasis on methodological approaches, predictive performance, and clinical applicability. Materials and
papers.summary: This review evaluates CT-based radiomics and radiogenomics for predicting molecular markers in clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC), finding these non-invasive methods promising for assessing tumor heterogeneity and guiding treatment. The authors highlight methodological approaches and predictive performance but note that clinical applicability remains limited by variability in study design and validation.

papers.title: A Length-Adaptive LLM-Enhanced Method for Drug-Target Interaction Prediction.
papers.abstract: Drug-target interaction (DTI) prediction is central to drug repurposing. Although existing methods integrate multi-dimensional features and have achieved certain progress, they rely heavily on molecular structure or graph structure information. This makes it difficult to capture complex biomedical semantic associations, leading to insufficient semantic information. To address this issue, this paper proposes BioLA-DTI, a large language model (LLM)-enhanced method for drug-target interaction prediction. The method leverages LLMs to provide semantic information for drugs and proteins. Furthermore
papers.summary: This paper introduces BioLA-DTI, a method that uses large language models to improve drug-target interaction prediction by capturing complex biomedical semantic associations, rather than relying solely on molecular or graph structures. The approach enhances prediction accuracy by leveraging LLMs to provide richer semantic information for both drugs and proteins.

papers.title: Design and Testing of an Integrated Robot for Harvesting, Stipe-Cutting, and Grading of Agaricus bisporus.
papers.abstract: To address the limitations of current Agaricus bisporus harvesting robots, including low picking efficiency, susceptibility to mechanical damage, poor operational stability, and discontinuous harvesting processes, an integrated robotic system capable of mushroom detection and localization, picking sequence planning, stipe-cutting, and grading was developed. The robot adopts a left-right symmetrical configuration and operates along the side of the mushroom cultivation racks. It mainly consists of a mobile platform, a lifting mechanism, dual picking units, a receiving unit, a stipe-cutting devic
papers.summary: This paper presents a new integrated robot for harvesting, stipe-cutting, and grading of Agaricus bisporus mushrooms, designed to improve picking efficiency and reduce mechanical damage. The robot features a symmetrical configuration with dual picking units and operates along cultivation racks, addressing limitations of current harvesting robots.

papers.title: Integration of Machine Learning-Based Pathogenicity Prediction and Phenotype Matching Improves Variant Prioritization in Rare Clinical Testing.
papers.abstract: Genome and exome sequencing have become central to diagnosing rare hereditary diseases, but each test returns thousands of variants that a clinical scientist must review by hand to find the one responsible for the patient's condition. This manual interpretation is the main bottleneck in clinical genomics. To reduce it, we developed DiagAI, a machine-learning system that ranks the variants found in a patient and returns a short list of the most likely causal candidates. DiagAI combines three sources of evidence: a pathogenicity score from the Universal Pathogenicity Predictor (UP2), a model we
papers.summary: The paper introduces DiagAI, a machine learning system that prioritizes disease-causing genetic variants by combining pathogenicity prediction with phenotype matching, aiming to reduce the manual review bottleneck in clinical genomics. By ranking variants from genome/exome sequencing, it helps clinicians focus on the most likely causal candidates for rare hereditary diseases.

papers.title: DeepExoMir: A Reproducible RNA Language Model Framework for CLIP-Seq-Supported MicroRNA Target-Site Prioritization.
papers.abstract: MicroRNAs regulate gene expression post-transcriptionally, yet target prediction faces a credibility gap: published methods drop sharply against CLIP-seq-validated negatives. We present DeepExoMir, a deep learning framework integrating frozen RiNALMo RNA language model embeddings with biologically informed features. Under a dual-probe ablation protocol on three miRBench test sets, DeepExoMir reaches mean AU-PRC 0.855, surpassing eight retrained baselines (paired bootstrap p<0.001). Evolutionary conservation and duplex structure prove largely redundant with language-model priors, motivating a s
papers.summary: DeepExoMir is a new deep learning framework that improves microRNA target prediction by combining RNA language model embeddings with biological features, achieving higher accuracy than existing methods when tested against CLIP-seq-validated data. The study finds that evolutionary conservation and duplex structure features add little beyond what the language model already captures, suggesting a simpler approach may suffice.

papers.title: Rapid Analysis of Caffeine, Protein and Trigonelline in Ugandan Arabica Coffee Using NIRS and Machine Learning Algorithms.
papers.abstract: Coffee is a major export earner for Uganda, raking in over USD 2 billion in 2025. The global price of coffee is tagged to the perceived quality in the cup which in turn is affected by the chemical composition of the green bean. Breeding for market-preferred Arabica coffee varieties is a major objective of coffee breeding programs. Determination of coffee bean chemical constituents is routinely done through expensive, slow and tedious laboratory procedures, making it unsustainable of resource-limited public sector coffee breeding programs. Here, we demonstrate the use of near-infrared spectrosc
papers.summary: This study shows that near-infrared spectroscopy (NIRS) combined with machine learning can rapidly and non-destructively measure key chemical compounds (caffeine, protein, trigonelline) in Ugandan Arabica coffee beans, replacing slow and expensive lab tests. This approach could make quality screening more accessible for resource-limited coffee breeding programs.

papers.title: NutriSteppe-AI: Development, Architecture, and Explainable Design of a Large Language Model-Driven Chatbot for Personalized Health Menu Generation.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Suboptimal dietary patterns are among the leading modifiable contributors to global morbidity and mortality, particularly in cardiovascular disease, type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), obesity, metabolic syndrome, and hypertension. Digital nutrition platforms have emerged to improve adherence to evidence-based dietary strategies; however, many systems lack structured optimization, processing-aware nutrient profiling, and explainable artificial intelligence (AI) mechanisms. The integration of large language models (LLMs) into digital health introduces conversational personal
papers.summary: This paper presents NutriSteppe-AI, a chatbot that uses large language models to generate personalized health menus, incorporating explainable AI to improve transparency in dietary recommendations. The system addresses limitations of existing digital nutrition platforms by adding structured optimization and nutrient profiling.

papers.title: Development of Machine Learning Models for Predicting Surgical Site Infection After Spinal Surgery.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Surgical site infection (SSI) remains a clinically important complication after spinal surgery. This study developed and assessed machine learning approaches for predicting postoperative SSI using routinely collected preoperative clinical variables, with emphasis on calibration and clinical applicability. Methods: In this retrospective single-center study, four prediction models were developed in patients undergoing spinal surgery: logistic regression, random forest, gradient boosting, and XGBoost. Model training used five-fold stratified cross-validation, and performanc
papers.summary: This study developed machine learning models (logistic regression, random forest, gradient boosting, XGBoost) to predict surgical site infection after spinal surgery using routine preoperative clinical data. The models were trained with cross-validation and evaluated for calibration and clinical applicability, offering a potential tool for risk stratification.

papers.title: Machine learning identifies neutrophil-related signatures for diagnostic value in neonatal sepsis.
papers.abstract: Neonatal sepsis (NS) is one of the leading causes of neonatal mortality. The nonspecific clinical manifestations and the limited timeliness of existing biomarkers (such as C-reactive protein) highlight the urgent need for highly accurate diagnostic tools. Neutrophils, as key effector cells of innate immunity, are closely involved in the progression of NS. This study integrated training (GSE69686) and validation (GSE25504) datasets from the GEO database. Neutrophil infiltration characteristics were analyzed utilizing CIBERSORT, and weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) was introd
papers.journal: Journal of clinical biochemistry and nutrition
papers.summary: This study uses machine learning to identify neutrophil-related gene signatures that could serve as diagnostic biomarkers for neonatal sepsis, addressing the need for more accurate and timely diagnostic tools. By analyzing public gene expression datasets, the authors found that neutrophil infiltration patterns and co-expressed gene modules can distinguish septic neonates from healthy controls.

papers.title: Adversarial Erasing Enhanced Multiple Instance Learning (siMILe): Discriminative Identification of Oligomeric Protein Structures in Single Molecule Localization Microscopy.
papers.abstract: Single-molecule localization microscopy (SMLM) achieves nanoscale imaging of complex protein structures in the cell. However, the ability to capture structural variability across cell conditions (cell lines, gene expression, treatment) from 3D point cloud SMLM data remains limited. We present siMILe, a weakly supervised multiple instance learning machine learning method to close this gap in interpretable subcellular discovery. siMILe identifies condition-specific changes in protein assemblies by leveraging their shape and network features, without requiring structure-level supervision. siMILe
papers.journal: Advanced intelligent systems (Weinheim an der Bergstrasse, Germany)
papers.summary: This paper introduces siMILe, a weakly supervised machine learning method that uses multiple instance learning to identify condition-specific changes in protein structures from 3D single-molecule localization microscopy data. The method can discriminate oligomeric protein assemblies based on shape and network features without requiring structure-level supervision, enabling discovery of structural variability across different cell conditions.

papers.title: Predicting the evolutionary and functional landscapes of viruses with a unified nucleotide-protein language model: LucaVirus.
papers.abstract: Predicting viral evolution and function remains a central challenge in biology, hindered by high sequence divergence and limited knowledge compared to cellular organisms. Here, we introduce LucaVirus, a multi-modal foundation model for viruses, trained on 25.4 billion nucleotide and amino acid tokens covering a vast majority of catalogued viral diversity. LucaVirus learns biologically meaningful representations that reflect relationships between sequences, protein/gene homology, and evolutionary divergence. Using these embeddings, we developed downstream models that address key virology tasks:
papers.summary: LucaVirus is a new AI model trained on billions of viral nucleotide and protein sequences that learns meaningful biological representations of viral evolution and function. It can predict relationships between sequences, protein homology, and evolutionary divergence, enabling downstream tasks in virology. This unified approach overcomes challenges posed by high sequence divergence in viruses.

papers.title: Novel plasma protein signatures for early diagnosis and prognostic stratification in colorectal cancer.
papers.abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) remains a major global health concern, underscoring the need for reliable biomarkers for diagnosis and prognosis. In this study, untargeted plasma proteomics was conducted across two cohorts comprising 321 participants in the discovery set and 353 in the validation set. Machine learning methods were employed to select biomarkers and develop diagnostic and prognostic models, with performance evaluated by the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). An eight-protein panel for CRC and a six-protein panel for advanced adenoma discriminated from healthy
papers.summary: This study identifies novel plasma protein signatures that can distinguish colorectal cancer and advanced adenoma from healthy individuals, using untargeted proteomics and machine learning across two large cohorts. The resulting protein panels show strong diagnostic performance, offering potential for early detection and prognostic stratification of colorectal cancer.

papers.title: A quality evaluation strategy for residual host cell proteins based on orthogonal analysis.
papers.abstract: Accurate quantification of host cell proteins (HCPs) is essential for the safety and quality control of biopharmaceuticals. Although enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) remains the current industry gold standard, heterogeneity among the polyclonal antibody repertoires of different commercial kits often results in substantial method-dependent bias. This study aimed to establish a novel strategy for the quality evaluation of HCP detection kits for biologics. Two Chinese hamster ovary cell-derived recombinant protein drug substances with different HCP burdens were utilized as model samples
papers.summary: This study develops a new strategy using orthogonal analysis to evaluate the quality of host cell protein (HCP) detection kits for biopharmaceuticals, addressing the bias caused by variability in commercial ELISA kits. By testing two Chinese hamster ovary cell-derived drug substances with different HCP levels, the approach aims to improve accuracy and reliability in HCP quantification for safety and quality control.

papers.title: Development and Interpretation of Machine Learning Models for Short-Term Functional Recovery and 90-Day Readmission in Patients with Cardiovascular Disease.
papers.abstract: Early prediction of functional recovery and post-discharge readmission may support multidisciplinary rehabilitation planning, follow-up stratification, and individualized management in patients with cardiovascular disease (CVD). This study aimed to develop and interpret machine learning (ML) models for predicting 1-week functional recovery and 90-day readmission.
papers.summary: This study developed machine learning models to predict short-term functional recovery and 90-day readmission in cardiovascular disease patients, aiming to improve rehabilitation planning and follow-up care. The models were interpreted to identify key predictors, potentially enabling more personalized patient management.

papers.title: Effective analysis of testicular seminoma toxicity and mechanisms of acetyl tributyl citrate using network toxicology, bulk RNA sequencing data, single-cell RNA sequencing data, and clinical data.
papers.abstract: Acetyl tributyl citrate (ATBC) is a widely used plasticizer ubiquitously present in the environment. Long-term high-dose ATBC exposure has been associated with reproductive system damage, yet its toxic effects and underlying mechanisms in testicular seminoma remain unclear. This study aimed to investigate the impact of ATBC on the prognosis of testicular seminoma.
papers.summary: This study investigates how the common plasticizer acetyl tributyl citrate (ATBC) affects testicular seminoma prognosis by integrating network toxicology, bulk and single-cell RNA sequencing, and clinical data. The findings reveal potential mechanisms of ATBC toxicity in this cancer type, highlighting its relevance to environmental exposures and male reproductive health.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence for early detection of diabetic retinopathy: A vision transformer-based approach.
papers.abstract: Early identification of diabetic retinopathy (DR), which is a primary cause of vision impairment globally, is a crucial phasis for effective intervention and treatment. Traditional screening workflows rely on manual diagnosis by ophthalmologists, which remains the gold standard but can be time-consuming and subject to variability due to human factors. To support and enhance the screening process, artificial intelligence (AI)-based tools have shown promise in automating DR detection, particularly with recent advances in deep learning. However, medical images with long-range dependencies and spa
papers.summary: This study presents a vision transformer-based AI model for early detection of diabetic retinopathy from retinal images, addressing limitations of traditional CNNs in capturing long-range spatial dependencies. The approach shows promise for automating screening workflows and reducing variability in manual diagnosis by ophthalmologists.

papers.title: Enhancing missense variant classification in predicted intrinsically disordered regions.
papers.abstract: Classifying disease-causing missense variants in intrinsically disordered regions (IDRs) remains a significant challenge, with over 25% of known deleterious variants occurring in these regions. Existing in silico missense variant predictors that predict variant classification generally perform better in ordered regions of the protein, limiting their effectiveness. To address this, we developed a machine learning methodology that integrates global IDR conformation (gIDRc) features from ALBATROSS, phase separation (PS) features from BioPython, and 1024-dimensional protein embeddings from ProtTra
papers.summary: This study presents a new machine learning method that improves the classification of disease-causing missense variants in intrinsically disordered regions (IDRs) of proteins, which are often poorly handled by existing tools. By integrating features from protein embeddings, disorder conformation, and phase separation predictions, the model achieves better performance for IDR variants. This addresses a key gap in variant effect prediction, as over 25% of known deleterious variants fall in these regions.

papers.title: Integrated post-GWAS, single-cell, and functional analyses prioritize TCTN2 at an osteoarthritis locus associated with innate immunity-related cartilage remodeling.
papers.abstract: Post-genome-wide association study (GWAS) interpretation of osteoarthritis (OA) increasingly requires integration with single-cell biology because many risk loci likely act through sterile inflammatory remodeling, regulatory and inflammatory chondrocyte states, and tissue-stress biology rather than through large disease-stage expression shifts. We therefore asked whether a published Transformer-based post-GWAS prioritization strategy could refine a multi-gene chr12 susceptibility locus into a tractable TCTN2-centered effector-gene hypothesis.
papers.summary: This study uses a Transformer-based post-GWAS prioritization strategy combined with single-cell data to refine a multi-gene osteoarthritis risk locus on chromosome 12, identifying TCTN2 as a likely effector gene involved in innate immunity-related cartilage remodeling. The approach highlights how integrating single-cell biology with GWAS can pinpoint specific genes in complex disease loci.

papers.title: Machine learning for chemotherapy decision-making in breast cancer using large language model.
papers.abstract: Breast cancer chemotherapy decision-making remains challenging due to biological heterogeneity and variability in clinical practice. This study proposes a hybrid framework integrating machine learning (ML), causal reasoning, and large language models (LLMs) to improve treatment recommendations.
papers.summary: This study develops a hybrid framework that combines machine learning, causal reasoning, and large language models to improve chemotherapy treatment recommendations for breast cancer patients. The approach aims to address challenges posed by biological heterogeneity and variable clinical practices in treatment decision-making.

papers.title: mwHIT: accelerated and accurate histone modification imputation using multi-scale window attention.
papers.abstract: Histone modifications regulate chromatin organization and gene activity, and abnormal modification patterns are closely associated with disease-related transcriptional dysregulation. Although ChIP-seq provides accurate measurements of histone modification profiles, genome-wide experimental profiling remains costly and time-consuming. Here, we propose mwHIT, a multi-scale window attention-based Histone Modification Imputation Transformer that predicts histone modification signals from run-on sequencing (RO-seq) and DNA sequence features. mwHIT captures both local and long-range regulatory infor
papers.summary: The authors present mwHIT, a deep learning model that uses multi-scale window attention to accurately predict histone modification signals from DNA sequence and run-on sequencing data, reducing the need for costly ChIP-seq experiments. The model captures both local and long-range regulatory information, enabling efficient genome-wide imputation of histone modification profiles.

papers.title: Deciphering tuberculosis pathway mechanisms via graph neural networks and multimodal deep learning: a comprehensive AI-driven framework for precision medicine.
papers.abstract: Tuberculosis (TB) remains a global health crisis, with complex molecular mechanisms that are not fully understood. Traditional pathway analysis methods fail to capture the intricate non-linear relationships within biological networks.
papers.summary: This paper presents a new AI framework that combines graph neural networks and multimodal deep learning to better understand the complex molecular pathways involved in tuberculosis. The approach aims to capture non-linear relationships in biological networks that traditional methods miss, potentially improving precision medicine for TB.

papers.title: S2DA-GO: enhancing protein function prediction via gradient-decoupled cross-attention and semantic priors.
papers.abstract: Accurate automated protein function prediction is essential for bridging the widening gap between the exponential accumulation of uncharacterized protein sequences and the limited repository of experimentally verified functional annotations. However, despite recent advances in incorporating Gene Ontology (GO) priors and sequence-label interactions, existing computational methods still face substantial challenges in long-tailed multi-label settings, particularly in handling optimization instability caused by rare-label noise and in learning reliable representations for sparsely annotated GO ter
papers.summary: This paper introduces S2DA-GO, a new deep learning method that improves protein function prediction by using a gradient-decoupled cross-attention mechanism and semantic priors from Gene Ontology. The approach addresses challenges with rare and sparsely annotated functions, achieving more stable optimization and better representation learning for long-tailed multi-label prediction tasks.

papers.title: What topological and geometric structure do biological foundation models learn? Evidence from 141 hypotheses.
papers.abstract: When biological foundation models like scGPT and Geneformer learn to process single-cell gene expression, what kind of geometric and topological structure forms in their internal representations? Is that structure biologically meaningful, or merely an artifact of training?. We address these questions through autonomous large-scale hypothesis screening: an AI-driven executor-brainstormer loop that proposed, tested, and refined 141 geometric and topological hypotheses across 52 iterations, covering persistent homology, manifold distances, cross-model alignment, community structure, directed topo
papers.summary: This study investigates the geometric and topological structures that emerge in the internal representations of biological foundation models (scGPT, Geneformer) trained on single-cell gene expression data. Using an AI-driven loop that autonomously proposed and tested 141 hypotheses, the authors find that these models learn biologically meaningful structures, such as persistent homology and manifold distances, rather than mere training artifacts.
